title: Cut elimination for \(\mu\mathrm{LK}_{p}^{+}\)
formal: For every finite sequent Gamma, does derivability of \(\vdash\Gamma\) in the arithmetic calculus \(\mu\mathrm{LK}_p^+\) imply derivability of the same sequent using its rules with cut removed?
definitions:
Terms have individual type iota with variables and constructors z:iota and s:iota→iota. Formulas use equality and disequality, the multiplicative connectives tensor, par and their units 1,bottom, additive conjunction &, disjunction plus and units top,0, first-order forall and exists, and positive least/greatest fixed points mu B and nu B of any finite predicate arity. There are no nonlogical predicate constants. Binding and predicate abstraction use simply typed lambda notation modulo alpha-beta-eta conversion. Fixed-point bodies are positive in the bound predicate. Write A^perp for De Morgan dual: interchange tensor/par, 1/bottom, &/plus, top/0, forall/exists, equality/disequality and mu/nu, dualizing the fixed-point body by substituting a dual predicate before taking the dual. Sequents are finite multisets, so exchange is implicit.

The rules, read as premises ⇒ conclusion, are: (i) Gamma,A,B ⇒ Gamma,A par B; (ii) Gamma ⇒ Gamma,bottom; (iii) Gamma,A and Delta,B ⇒ Gamma,Delta,A tensor B; (iv) the zero-premise sequent 1; (v) Gamma,A and Gamma,B ⇒ Gamma,A & B; (vi) the zero-premise sequent Gamma,top; (vii) Gamma,A_i ⇒ Gamma,A_0 plus A_1. There is no introduction rule for additive 0. Equality has the zero-premise sequent t=t. Disequality concludes Gamma,t≠u from Gamma theta when theta is a most general first-order unifier of t,u; if they are not unifiable it has no premise. Substitution applies to the whole context.

Universal introduction is Gamma,B(y) ⇒ Gamma,forall x B(x), with fresh individual y absent from the conclusion; existential introduction is Gamma,B(t) ⇒ Gamma,exists x B(x). Least-fixed-point unfolding is Gamma,B(mu B)(t-vector) ⇒ Gamma,(mu B)(t-vector). Greatest-fixed-point introduction has premises Gamma,S(t-vector) and B(S)(x-vector),S(x-vector)^perp, and conclusion Gamma,(nu B)(t-vector), where S is a formula-valued predicate abstraction of the matching arity and x-vector consists of fresh distinct individual variables. The fixed-point identity axiom is (mu B)(t-vector),(nu B^dual)(t-vector), with no premises.

Both calculi also allow weakening Gamma ⇒ Gamma,A and contraction Gamma,A,A ⇒ Gamma,A for every formula. Only the plus calculus additionally allows cut, from Gamma,A and Delta,A^perp to Gamma,Delta. Derivations are finite trees using these rules and arbitrary legal coinvariants S. No semantic arithmetic axioms, cyclic derivations or infinite proof trees are added. The cut-free target may use entirely different coinvariants and need not arise by a specified local reduction procedure.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked admissibility theorem for cut for the displayed calculus, or one sequent with a finite proof using cut and a proof that no finite cut-free derivation exists. Consistency, arithmetic interpretation or cut elimination for the underlying linear system alone does not establish this theorem.
context: Manighetti and Miller add unrestricted weakening and contraction, as well as cut, to their fixed-point linear calculus. Their paper proves consistency and an arithmetic embedding but explicitly leaves cut elimination unsettled.
why: Cut elimination would establish a fundamental proof-theoretic property of arithmetic with fixed points.

import_provenance.original_title: Cut elimination for classical fixed-point arithmetic μLK_p⁺
import_provenance.original_statement: Does every proof in Manighetti–Miller’s μLK_p⁺ admit a cut-free proof of the same sequent? The system adds unrestricted weakening and contraction to first-order μMALL with equality and least/greatest fixed points; consistency and an embedding of Peano arithmetic are known, but eliminating intermediate lemmas remains open.

context_blocks.text: Manighetti and Miller add unrestricted weakening and contraction, as well as cut, to their fixed-point linear calculus. Their paper proves consistency and an arithmetic embedding but explicitly leaves cut elimination unsettled.

sentences: The system extends polarized fixed-point linear arithmetic with weakening and contraction.
Cut allows an intermediate formula and its dual to be eliminated between two derivations.
The question asks whether every resulting sequent already has a finite cut-free proof.
Coinvariants remain unrestricted within the specified formula language.
Consistency and an embedding of Peano arithmetic do not imply cut admissibility.
